newsitem.title: UK: UK's Nationwide says Aug house prices up 1.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: UK's Nationwide says Aug house prices up 1.7 pct.

text.p: The Nationwide Building Society released the following UK house price data -
HOUSE PRICES (index base Q1 1983=100) Aug July Aug,95
NOTE - The Nationwide said prices are at their highest level since August 1991.
Nationwide's corporate development manager Philip Williamson said the statistics provide further evidence of recovery in the housing market.
"With steady increases expected to continue into the autumn, we will see house prices at the end of this year at least 5.0 percent higher than at the end of 1995."

A spokesman told Reuters that while the Nationwide was sticking to its official forecast that house prices will end the year 5.0 percent higher than 1995, the rise will probably be slightly above that level.
Williamson said the low number of transactions remained disappointing. "The market is still suffering from a shortage of quality property for sale, particularly for mid- to higher-priced property."
Supply shortages are most pronounced in the south-east of England following the pattern of previous recoveries.
But Williamson said the market was not seeing a boom.

"We still feel that any talk of a damaging boom is seriously misplaced. With increased house prices eroding negative equity and generally freeing up activity, sustainable and orderly growth will continue to return to the market."
The Nationwide forecasts house prices will rise by 6.0 percent in 1997 and by 8.0 percent in 1998.
